pretexts: fraudster claims to be from bank or credit card provider about unauthorized charges
fraudster claims to be from Amazon about account compromise
fraudster claims computer has virus or has been hacked
fraudster claims to be from Microsoft or computer company
fraudster claims to be from government agency or law enforcement offering to recover stolen money
fraudster claims CAFC is investigating and victim must cooperate to catch suspect
fraudster claims victim must help with sting operation
emerging_tactics: fraudulent letters with CAFC logo and letterhead

kill_chain_signals.contact: unsolicited telephone calls, alarming website pop-ups, fraudsters send fraudulent letter via email
kill_chain_signals.pretext: claim unauthorized charges on account, computer infected with virus, CAFC is investigating and victim must cooperate, promise to get money back from previous fraud
kill_chain_signals.payment: demand money for reimbursement fees or as bait money, claim payment is required to assist with investigation
kill_chain_signals.movement: fraudsters request remote access to computer, provide fraudulent contact information for victim to communicate with them
kill_chain_signals.cashout: promise to return funds but never will

red_flags: CAFC or police will never ask to transfer money or make a payment
CAFC or police will never ask for remote access to your computer
CAFC or police will never ask for personal information or any type of payment
Fraudsters often provide first 4 to 6 numbers of debit or credit card
Criminals use call-spoofing to mislead victims
